name: Hong Kong
capital: Hong Kong (Special Administrative Region of China)
tagline: British-style degrees, published IB requirements, and rising fees
summary: Hong Kong is the most legible system on this list for an IB student. The universities teach in English, publish their entry requirements in IB points, run a clearly signposted non-JUPAS route for applicants with international qualifications, and accept applications on a rolling basis well past the IB results date. Degrees are four years, the first of which is broad in an American way before you narrow. The honest problem is cost: non-local fees have climbed steeply, and for 2027/28 HKU is charging HK$250,000–280,000 a year and HKUST HK$260,000. That is genuinely expensive — comparable to a private American university before aid. If you can get one of the entrance scholarships, Hong Kong is outstanding value; if you cannot, it is one of the priciest options here.
whyConsider: Deadlines actually work for IB students. HKU's first round closes 25 November 2026 and then reviews on a rolling basis until 25 August 2027; HKUST's priority round is 25 November 2026 with applications open until 30 June 2027. You can apply before and after results.
IB requirements are published and concrete — CUHK states a minimum of 30 points out of 45 for non-local applicants.
Everything is taught in English, the degree structure is British-derived, and credit transfer and exchange to Europe are routine.
Five universities in a small territory, all research-intensive, all internationally ranked, all reachable by metro.

All three of the top universities run substantial merit scholarships for international entrants — HKUST alone lists an Admissions Scholarship, a Global Learners Scholarship, a Beyond Academic Admissions Scholarship and a new Future Leaders Award.
watchOuts: Fees are the headline risk. HKU 2027/28: HK$280,000 a year for STEM programmes, HK$250,000 for non-STEM, HK$590,000 for medicine and dentistry. HKUST: HK$260,000. CUHK: HK$230,000. On top of that, budget HK$60,000–100,000 a year for accommodation and living.

Over a four-year degree that is roughly HK$1.0–1.3 million in tuition alone — about DKK 900,000 to 1.1 million at recent rates. Without a scholarship this is the most expensive option in this whole dataset apart from the American branch campuses.

The first round in late November 2026 is the one that matters. HKU and HKUST both make offers from late December onwards, and the good scholarships are allocated early. Applying in the rolling window after results is possible but competitively worse.
Hong Kong's four-year degree means an extra year compared with a three-year Danish, Dutch or British bachelor's — factor that into the total cost.
We could not verify PolyU or CityU fees, requirements or deadlines from official pages. Those figures are left blank here on purpose.
Housing on campus is not guaranteed for all four years at every university, and the private rental market in Hong Kong is among the most expensive in the world.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: CUHK: 30 points out of 45 for non-local applicants. HKU and HKUST list the IB as an accepted qualification but publish requirements programme by programme rather than as a single minimum.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Programme-specific. Subject preferences vary and CUHK publishes an IB subject guide. Engineering and science programmes normally expect HL Mathematics and a relevant HL science; medicine expects HL Chemistry and Biology.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No conversion — IB points are read directly.
notes: The route for a Danish IB student is the 'non-JUPAS' or 'international qualifications' route. JUPAS is the domestic system for Hong Kong DSE students and is not relevant to you.

HKU states that admission decisions rest on academic performance plus interview performance, personal statement, references and other submitted documents — it is a holistic process, not a points threshold.
Predicted grades carry the early rounds; final offers are conditional on the July diploma.
The IB is normally accepted as proof of English. HKUST lists the IB among acceptable English language qualifications.

portal.name: No central portal for non-JUPAS applicants — apply direct to each university

deadlines.label: HKU — first round
deadlines.notes: Applications received after this are reviewed on a rolling basis.

deadlines.label: HKU — final deadline
deadlines.notes: Well after IB results are published on 6 July 2027, so a late application is possible — but the best programmes and scholarships will already be allocated.

deadlines.label: HKUST — priority round
deadlines.notes: Offers are announced from late December 2026 onwards. Applications after 26 November are considered on a rolling basis.

deadlines.label: HKUST — application closes
deadlines.notes: Closes before IB results day on 6 July 2027, so you must apply on predicted grades.

deadlines.label: CUHK, PolyU and CityU non-local rounds
deadlines.notes: Not verified from official pages in this research. Check each university's non-JUPAS admissions page from September 2026.

steps: In September or October 2026, shortlist programmes and note that Hong Kong applications are to specific programmes, not to a faculty.
Get predicted grades from your IB coordinator in good time for the 25 November 2026 first rounds at HKU and HKUST — this round carries the offers and the scholarships.
Apply direct through each university's own online system, paying a separate application fee to each.
Apply for scholarships where they need a separate application — HKUST's Beyond Academic Admissions Scholarship and Future Leaders Award are application-based rather than automatic.
Expect an interview, usually online, for the more selective programmes; HKU explicitly weighs interview performance.
Accept your offer and apply for a student visa through the university, which acts as your sponsor to the Immigration Department. Allow six to eight weeks.
Apply for hall accommodation as soon as you have an offer — it is allocated separately and is much cheaper than renting.
application.selectionNotes: Holistic and competitive. HKU, CUHK and HKUST are the three most selective; PolyU and CityU are strong in applied and professional fields and somewhat more accessible. Because the non-local pool is separate from the JUPAS pool, a good IB student is competing in a smaller field than the raw rankings suggest.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Essentially all of them. English is the medium of instruction at HKU, HKUST, PolyU and CityU; CUHK is formally bilingual but teaches most programmes in English.
language.englishProof: IB English is normally accepted. HKUST lists the IB among acceptable English language qualifications; other universities set IELTS or TOEFL alternatives.
notes: Cantonese is the language of the street and of most student social life. You do not need it to study, but not having it will keep you inside the international bubble.
CUHK's bilingual policy means a small number of courses are taught in Cantonese or Putonghua — check the medium of instruction for your specific programme.

tuitionEuEea.value: Hong Kong does not differentiate by EU status. The categories are 'local' and 'non-local'; a Danish student is non-local. See tuitionNonEu.

tuitionNonEu.value: HKU 2027/28: HK$280,000 per year for STEM programmes, HK$250,000 for non-STEM, HK$590,000 for MBBS and BDS. HKUST 2027/28: HK$260,000 per year (about USD 33,000). CUHK 2027/28: HK$230,000 per year. PolyU and CityU not verified.

livingCostMonthly.value: Annual rather than monthly. HKU: residential halls and colleges HK$17,290–37,940 a year (285 days, excluding the summer semester), off-campus housing HK$30,000–50,000 a year, general living expenses up to HK$50,000 a year. HKUST: university accommodation about HK$21,000–51,000 a residential year, personal expenses about HK$60,000 a year. CUHK: on-campus accommodation about HK$17,000 and living expenses about HK$45,000 a year.

notes: CUHK's own published total, tuition plus on-campus accommodation plus living, is roughly HK$292,000 a year — the cheapest of the three verified universities.
These are 2027/28 figures, which is exactly the year a May 2027 IB cohort would start. That is unusually good data; treat it as reliable.
Hong Kong fees have risen sharply in recent years. Budget on the assumption of further increases across a four-year degree, even though some universities fix the entry-year rate.
Hall accommodation is dramatically cheaper than the private market and is the single biggest lever on your real cost.

funding: HKU merit scholarships — a broad range of merit-based awards with one-off payments and renewable support for tuition and living expenses, found through HKU's scholarship finder. Most are awarded from the admission application.

HKUST scholarships — the University Admissions Scholarship for Other Qualifications and the Global Learners Scholarship are merit-based and awarded from the admission; the Beyond Academic Admissions Scholarship and the new Future Leaders Award require a separate application. HKUST also notes that need-based financial aid is available through its Scholarship and Financial Aid Office.
CUHK and the other universities run comparable entrance scholarship schemes; details not verified in this research.
The Hong Kong government's Belt and Road Scholarship and HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund exist but are largely targeted at specific partner countries — check current eligibility for EU citizens.
Danish SU: a full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules. Check su.dk before budgeting.
Given the fee level, a scholarship is not a nice extra in Hong Kong — for most Danish families it is the difference between viable and not. Apply for everything, and apply in the first round.
workRights: Non-local students at UGC-funded institutions may take on-campus part-time work and, under the Immigration Department's arrangements, certain off-campus internships and summer jobs. The rules are narrower than in Europe and were not re-verified from an official page in this research — confirm with the Hong Kong Immigration Department before relying on earnings.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. Your university sponsors a student visa application to the Hong Kong Immigration Department once you accept an offer; allow six to eight weeks. You must enter Hong Kong on that visa, not as a visitor. On arrival, apply for a Hong Kong Identity Card within 30 days.
housing: Halls of residence are the standard first-year route and are much cheaper than renting — HK$17,000–38,000 a year at HKU against HK$30,000–50,000 off campus. Places are allocated separately from the admission and are not guaranteed for all four years at every university; some universities allocate later years on a points system tied to hall participation. Apply the day your offer arrives.
healthcare: Non-local students are normally required to hold medical insurance, often arranged through the university as a compulsory charge. Public healthcare in Hong Kong is available to non-residents at a higher non-eligible-persons rate, which is substantial for anything serious. Your Danish EHIC does not apply. Check what the university's scheme covers and top it up.

institutions.name: The University of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes. Broad four-year curriculum across arts, business, engineering, law, medicine, science and social sciences.
institutions.note: The oldest and most internationally recognised university in Hong Kong, with a world-leading dental school. Its first round closes 25 November 2026 and it then reviews on a rolling basis until 25 August 2027, which is the most IB-friendly calendar in this dataset. 2027/28 fees: HK$280,000 STEM, HK$250,000 non-STEM, HK$590,000 medicine and dentistry.

institutions.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: Most programmes are taught in English; CUHK is formally bilingual and a minority of courses use Cantonese or Putonghua.
institutions.note: A collegiate university on a green hillside campus above Tolo Harbour — the only one in Hong Kong with a genuine residential college system. Publishes a clear IB minimum of 30 points out of 45 and the lowest verified non-local fee of the big three, HK$230,000 for 2027/28.

institutions.name: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes: science, engineering, business and management, humanities and social science, and interdisciplinary programmes.
institutions.note: Young, science-and-business focused, on the most spectacular campus in Asia overlooking Clear Water Bay. 2027/28 fee HK$260,000. Priority round 25 November 2026, offers from late December, applications close 30 June 2027 — before IB results, so predicted grades are essential.

institutions.name: The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, with particular depth in design, engineering, hotel and tourism management, and health sciences.
institutions.note: The most applied and professional of the Hong Kong universities. Its School of Design (in the Zaha Hadid-designed Jockey Club Innovation Tower) and its School of Hotel and Tourism Management are both world-ranked. Fees and deadlines not verified — check directly.

institutions.name: City University of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, including business, engineering, data science, creative media, law and veterinary medicine.
institutions.note: Hong Kong's fastest-rising university, with the territory's only veterinary school (founded with Cornell) and a strong School of Creative Media. Sits directly on top of a metro station and a shopping centre. Fees and deadlines not verified.

institutions.name: Hong Kong Baptist University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, with strengths in communication and journalism, Chinese medicine, business and the creative arts.
institutions.note: Smaller and more liberal-arts in feel than the big five, with the best-regarded journalism and communication school in the region and a strong Academy of Film. A good fit if the draw is media rather than engineering.

institutions.name: Lingnan University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes. Hong Kong's designated liberal arts university, with a small, residential, seminar-based model.
institutions.note: Hong Kong's liberal arts university, and the only one that guarantees residential places to essentially all undergraduates. Small classes, compulsory community service, and the closest thing in the territory to a European university college. Considerably more accessible than HKU or CUHK.

institutions.name: The Education University of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: Education degrees and a growing set of non-teaching programmes in language studies, psychology and social sciences.
institutions.note: The specialist teacher-education university, consistently ranked in the world top twenty for education. Narrow in scope, but if you want to teach, this is the address in Asia.

institutions.name: The Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: BFA and BMus degrees in dance, drama, film and television, music, theatre and entertainment arts, and Chinese opera.
institutions.note: Asia's leading conservatoire for the performing arts, in a landmark building on the Wan Chai waterfront. Audition and portfolio entry, and the only route on this list where IB points matter less than what you can do in the room.

institutions.name: The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: Business, communication, decision sciences, translation and social science degrees, taught in English.
institutions.note: A private, teaching-focused university with small classes and a business orientation, on a residential campus in Sha Tin. Lower entry requirements than the public universities and considerably cheaper, but with less research weight behind the name.

institutions.name: Hong Kong Metropolitan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied degrees in business, nursing, creative arts, science and technology, with both full-time and distance routes.
institutions.note: Formerly the Open University of Hong Kong, now a full self-financing university with a strong nursing school and a practical, career-facing curriculum. The most accessible route into Hong Kong higher education.

institutions.name: Hong Kong Shue Yan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Journalism and communication, psychology, law and business studies, with teaching in English and Chinese.
institutions.note: Hong Kong's first private university, small and teaching-focused, with a well-regarded journalism department. Check the medium of instruction for your specific programme before applying.

institutions.name: Technological and Higher Education Institute of Hong Kong
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied bachelor's degrees in horticulture and landscape, fashion design, food science, surveying, hospitality and testing science.
institutions.note: Part of the Vocational Training Council, with unusually specific applied degrees you will not find at the research universities — horticulture, testing and certification science, fashion. Worth knowing about if your interest is narrow and practical.
